introduction: South Carolina’s earned income credit is claimed with the state tax return using TC-60 for the correct tax year. It is a nonrefundable state credit.
description: South Carolina’s earned income credit is claimed with the state tax return using TC-60 for the correct tax year. It is a nonrefundable state credit.

sections.who: Revenue lists full-year South Carolina residents who claim federal EITC as eligible.
sections.get: For 2023 and later years, the state rate is 125 percent of federal EITC. A nonrefundable credit cannot reduce state tax below zero; the state lists no carryforward.
sections.docs:
• Federal return and EITC calculation.
  • State residency and income records.
  • Correct-year TC-60 and required state schedules.
sections.apply:
1. Get the correct form

    Use Revenue’s credit listing.

  2. Calculate the credit

    Follow TC-60 and the state return instructions.

  3. File with the return

    Include required schedules and save the calculation.
sections.after: Keep return copies and ask a tax preparer or Revenue about a disputed calculation.
sections.sources: Checked October 1, 2026 using Current EIC eligibility and rate, Nonrefundable-credit rules. USA Assistance background guide. Program staff determine eligibility and available assistance.

faqs: Is it a cash refund beyond tax owed?
It is nonrefundable, so it cannot reduce state tax below zero.
Can part-year residents claim this state credit?
Revenue lists full-year residents for this credit.
The state credit listing says no carryforward.
